Let the top vertex be \(D\), and let the other two base vertices be \(B\) and \(C\). Thus \(ABC\) is the base face of the tetrahedron.

Let \(M\) and \(N\) be the midpoints of \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively. These are the two midpoint vertices of the shaded triangular cutting plane \(DMN\).

The portion containing \(A\) is the tetrahedron \(ADMN\). Its base is \(\triangle AMN\), while the original tetrahedron has base \(\triangle ABC\).

Since
\[
AM=\frac12 AB,\qquad AN=\frac12 AC,
\]
the triangle \(AMN\) is similar to \(ABC\) with scale factor \(\frac12\). Therefore,
\[
\frac{[\triangle AMN]}{[\triangle ABC]}=\left(\frac12\right)^2=\frac14.
\]

The two tetrahedra have the same altitude from \(D\) to the base plane, so their volumes have the same ratio:
\[
\frac{V_{ADMN}}{V_{ABCD}}=\frac14.
\]

Hence the required volume is
\[
V_{ADMN}=\frac14(120)=\boxed{30}.
\]
